dedupe_keys.name: chlorine supply interruption after the 2021 westlake chemical transformer failure washington state department of health

description: This Washington State Department of Health page records the state response when Westlake Chemical in Longview, Washington, suffered a critical production failure of chlorine and sodium hydroxide, chemicals essential to drinking water and wastewater utilities, after a transformer failed in 2021. The page states that drinking water remained safe, asks customers to limit outdoor use to stretch supply, says a replacement transformer had arrived with production expected to resume on 28 June, and notes that some utilities had on-site chlorine generators or several weeks of stock while the department was still assessing smaller utilities. It describes utilities inventorying needs statewide and preparing to share remaining supply through mutual aid, and gives preparation guidance. Coverage: one state and one supplier failure; a web page, not a report. Access: free, with the licence not stated. Caveats: written mid-event, so it does not give final shortages or costs. It supports single-supplier dependency, mutual aid and chemical inventory studies, and relates to the EPA supply chain case studies and the TCEQ Winter Storm Uri review in the catalogue.
